verses.1: When you enter the land that the LORD your God gives you as an inheritance and you take possession of it and settle in it,
verses.2: take the first of all the fruit of the soil that you bring from your land, which the LORD your God gives you, and put it in a basket. Then go to the place that the LORD your God chooses to establish His name there.
verses.3: You will go to the priest who will be in charge in those days and say to him, "I declare today to the LORD my God that I have entered the land which the LORD swore to our ancestors to give us."
verses.4: The priest will take the basket from your hand and place it before the altar of the LORD your God.
verses.5: Then you will respond and say before the LORD your God, "A wandering Aramean was my father, and he went down to Egypt and lived there as a sojourner, few in number. But there he became a great and mighty nation, numerous and strong.
verses.6: "The Egyptians treated us harshly, oppressed us, and imposed hard labor on us.
verses.7: "We cried out to the LORD, the God of our ancestors, and the LORD heard our voice and saw our affliction, our toil, and our oppression.
verses.8: "The LORD brought us out of Egypt with a strong hand, with an outstretched arm, with great terror and with signs and wonders.
verses.9: "He brought us to this place and gave us this land, a land flowing with milk and honey.
verses.10: "Now, behold, I bring the first of the fruit of the soil, which You, O LORD, have given me—a land flowing with milk and honey. I have set it before the LORD your God. And I will bow down before the LORD your God.
verses.11: "You shall rejoice in all the good things that the LORD your God has given you, you and your household, you and the Levite, and the sojourner who is among you."
verses.12: When you have finished tithing all your tithes in the third year, the year of tithing, you must give it to the Levite, to the sojourner, to the orphan, and to the widow, so that they may eat in your towns and be satisfied.
verses.13: Then you shall say before the LORD your God, "I have removed the sacred portion from my house and also given it to the Levite, to the sojourner, to the orphan, and to the widow, as You commanded me. I have not transgressed Your commandments, nor have I forgotten.
verses.14: "I have not eaten of it in mourning, nor have I set it aside in uncleanness, nor have I given any of it to the dead. I have listened to the voice of the LORD my God; I have done just as You commanded me."
verses.15: "Look down from Your holy dwelling in heaven, and bless Your people Israel and the land which You gave us, as You swore to our ancestors, a land flowing with milk and honey."
verses.16: On this day the LORD your God commands you to observe these statutes and judgments. You must keep them and do them with all your heart and with all your soul.
verses.17: You have declared today that the LORD is your God, that you will walk in His ways, and that you will keep His statutes, His commandments, and His judgments, and that you will listen to His voice.
verses.18: And the LORD has declared you today to be His special possession, just as He spoke, to keep all His commandments.
verses.19: "To make you the head and not the tail, and to be only at the top and not at the bottom. And to be a holy people to the LORD your God, as He has spoken."

notes:
Notes
- v. 5: "A wandering Aramean was my father" — the Hebrew אֲרַמִּי אֹבֵד אָבִי is traditionally rendered as "a wandering Aramean was my father," referring to Jacob or Abraham, depending on the interpretation. The translation follows the literal text.
- v. 10: "land flowing with milk and honey" — this is a standard expression for a fertile land, used in several places in Deuteronomy. It is rendered consistently with the phrase in v. 9.
- v. 19: "To make you the head and not the tail..." — the Hebrew is metaphorical and is rendered in a way that preserves the imagery without relying on standard English phrasing of the concept.
raw:
[1] When you enter the land that the LORD your God gives you as an inheritance and you take possession of it and settle in it,

[2] take the first of all the fruit of the soil that you bring from your land, which the LORD your God gives you, and put it in a basket. Then go to the place that the LORD your God chooses to establish His name there.

[3] You will go to the priest who will be in charge in those days and say to him, "I declare today to the LORD my God that I have entered the land which the LORD swore to our ancestors to give us."

[4] The priest will take the basket from your hand and place it before the altar of the LORD your God.

[5] Then you will respond and say before the LORD your God, "A wandering Aramean was my father, and he went down to Egypt and lived there as a sojourner, few in number. But there he became a great and mighty nation, numerous and strong.

[6] "The Egyptians treated us harshly, oppressed us, and imposed hard labor on us.

[7] "We cried out to the LORD, the God of our ancestors, and the LORD heard our voice and saw our affliction, our toil, and our oppression.

[8] "The LORD brought us out of Egypt with a strong hand, with an outstretched arm, with great terror and with signs and wonders.

[9] "He brought us to this place and gave us this land, a land flowing with milk and honey.

[10] "Now, behold, I bring the first of the fruit of the soil, which You, O LORD, have given me—a land flowing with milk and honey. I have set it before the LORD your God. And I will bow down before the LORD your God.

[11] "You shall rejoice in all the good things that the LORD your God has given you, you and your household, you and the Levite, and the sojourner who is among you."

[12] When you have finished tithing all your tithes in the third year, the year of tithing, you must give it to the Levite, to the sojourner, to the orphan, and to the widow, so that they may eat in your towns and be satisfied.

[13] Then you shall say before the LORD your God, "I have removed the sacred portion from my house and also given it to the Levite, to the sojourner, to the orphan, and to the widow, as You commanded me. I have not transgressed Your commandments, nor have I forgotten.

[14] "I have not eaten of it in mourning, nor have I set it aside in uncleanness, nor have I given any of it to the dead. I have listened to the voice of the LORD my God; I have done just as You commanded me."

[15] "Look down from Your holy dwelling in heaven, and bless Your people Israel and the land which You gave us, as You swore to our ancestors, a land flowing with milk and honey."

[16] On this day the LORD your God commands you to observe these statutes and judgments. You must keep them and do them with all your heart and with all your soul.

[17] You have declared today that the LORD is your God, that you will walk in His ways, and that you will keep His statutes, His commandments, and His judgments, and that you will listen to His voice.

[18] And the LORD has declared you today to be His special possession, just as He spoke, to keep all His commandments.

[19] "To make you the head and not the tail, and to be only at the top and not at the bottom. And to be a holy people to the LORD your God, as He has spoken."

Notes
- v. 5: "A wandering Aramean was my father" — the Hebrew אֲרַמִּי אֹבֵד אָבִי is traditionally rendered as "a wandering Aramean was my father," referring to Jacob or Abraham, depending on the interpretation. The translation follows the literal text.
- v. 10: "land flowing with milk and honey" — this is a standard expression for a fertile land, used in several places in Deuteronomy. It is rendered consistently with the phrase in v. 9.
- v. 19: "To make you the head and not the tail..." — the Hebrew is metaphorical and is rendered in a way that preserves the imagery without relying on standard English phrasing of the concept.
